summary: Hardened /tmp and /dev/shm with nosuid,nodev,noexec and verified persistence through a node1 reboot. Existing data, permissions, services, OS release, and kernel were preserved.
actions_performed: Configured /tmp as a persistent self-bind mount to preserve existing contents.
Validated /etc/fstab with no errors or warnings.
Behaviorally verified noexec, nosuid, and nodev on both paths before and after reboot.
Restarted node1 once, confirmed its boot ID changed, and verified complete recovery.
Removed test artifacts and the temporary rollback copy.

evidence.summary: Shows valid fstab entries for both paths, effective nosuid,nodev,noexec options, and clean final validation.

evidence.requirement: Execution, setuid behavior, and device nodes are blocked on both paths
evidence.summary: Baseline demonstrated these behaviors were previously allowed; pre- and post-reboot tests show execution denied, setuid ignored, and device opens denied on both filesystems.
Captures healthy baseline with boot ID 739c9792-..., reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID db246150-..., running system, active services, SSH listener, and recovered hardened mounts.
Confirms RHEL 10.0 and the original 6.12.0-55.9.1 kernel remain installed, expected data remains, boot-created systemd private directories explain volatile /tmp metadata, and no test residue remains.
